# DynaLM: Local LLM Engine for CPU and GPU

> DynaLM is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) program that runs large language models (LLMs) on your own
> computer, on the CPU or the GPU, fully offline. It is one small C++20 program: no Python, no cloud
> account, no telemetry. It runs Llama, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek-R1-Distill, Mistral, Phi and IBM Granite
> models as a terminal chat or as an OpenAI-compatible API server. It is an alternative to Ollama and
> llama.cpp for Linux, macOS and Windows (x64 and ARM64).

## Key facts
- **What it does:** runs open-weight AI models locally (`dynalm run`, `dynalm serve`) with familiar
  commands (`pull`, `run`, `serve`).
- **CPU support:**
  - AVX2, AVX-512 and AMX on Intel and AMD;
  - NEON on Apple Silicon, ARM64 Linux and Windows on ARM.
- **GPU support (preview):**
  - Apple Metal (Apple Silicon);
  - Vulkan (AMD, Intel, NVIDIA and Qualcomm GPUs);
  - NVIDIA CUDA.
- **Automatic device choice:** `--backend auto` uses the GPU when it can run the model, otherwise the
  CPU. `--backend cpu|metal|vulkan|cuda` forces one device.
- **Serving:**
  - continuous batching, chunked prefill;
  - paged KV cache with prefix sharing and copy-on-write;
  - speculative decoding;
  - Prometheus metrics.
- **API:** OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` (streaming), `/v1/completions` and `/v1/models`.
  It works with the OpenAI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM, Open WebUI, Continue.dev and Cursor.
- **Security:** loopback by default, and an API key (`--api-key-file`) for network use.
- **Formats:** GGUF, SafeTensors, GPTQ, AWQ.
- **Quantization:** Q2_K–Q8_0, F16, BF16, F32 (`Q4_K_M` recommended).

## Measured results (Apple Silicon GPU, Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M, vs llama.cpp server)
- Memory, one user: 390 MB vs 1,113 MB (about 3× less).
- Typical time to first token with 4–8 users: 1.9–2.5× faster.
- Single-user speed: about 7 ms per token, within about 10% of llama.cpp.
- llama.cpp has higher total throughput with 8+ simultaneous users.

## Install
- Linux and macOS: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`
- Windows (x64 and ARM64): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex`
- Docker: `docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 -v "$PWD/models:/models" ghcr.io/dynalm-project/dynalm:cpu serve /models/model.gguf --allow-unauthenticated`
- GPU builds: `cmake --preset macos-metal`, `linux-vulkan`, `linux-cuda`, `msvc-vulkan` or `msvc-cuda`.
- Check a machine: `dynalm doctor`.

## Commands
- `dynalm pull <model>`: download a model by name or Hugging Face path.
- `dynalm run <model>`: chat in the terminal; `-p "<prompt>"` asks one question.
- `dynalm serve <model>`: OpenAI-compatible server on http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1.
- `dynalm models`, `dynalm models --available`, `dynalm models rm <model>`: manage models.
- `dynalm inspect <model>`: architecture and memory needs.
- `dynalm benchmark <model>`: measure speed.
- `dynalm stop`: stop a running server.

## Ollama to DynaLM
- `ollama pull` → `dynalm pull`
- `ollama run` → `dynalm run`
- `ollama list` → `dynalm models`
- `ollama rm` → `dynalm models rm`
- `ollama show` → `dynalm inspect`
- `ollama serve` → `dynalm serve`

## Model catalog
- `qwen2.5:1.5b`: 1.1 GB, best starting point, runs on CPU and GPU.
- `qwen2.5:0.5b`: 491 MB, fast chat on small PCs, runs on CPU and GPU.
- `qwen3:4b`: 2.5 GB, best quality in the catalog.
- `qwen3:0.6b`: 639 MB, small reasoning model.
- `qwen3:1.7b`: 1.8 GB, small reasoning model.
- `llama3.2:1b`: 808 MB, fast chat.
- `llama3.2:3b`: 2.0 GB, writing and coding.
- `gemma3:270m`: 292 MB, very small.
- `gemma3:1b`: 806 MB, general chat.
- `phi3.5:3.8b`: 2.4 GB, maths and code.
- `granite3.1-moe:1b`: 822 MB, mixture-of-experts.
- `smollm2:135m`: 145 MB, testing.
